predecessors.name: Dutch Formosa
predecessors.text: the Dutch East India Company's Taiwan, ruled 'from Fort Zeelandia (Tayouan)'; the Dutch 'ended ... rule over Taiwan' on 1 February 1662

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: Taiwan and Penghu: 'Taiwan was then formally annexed in April 1684' as Taiwan Prefecture of Fujian

capitals.name: Anping (Fort Zeelandia, present-day Tainan), with the Eastern Capital (Dongdu) at Chikan

ledger.x: 7 April 1661: the siege of Fort Zeelandia begins.
February 1662: Taiwan passes from the Dutch East India Company to the Zheng.
November 1663: the Qing, helped by the Dutch, take Xiamen and Kinmen.
1674: Zheng Jing joins the Revolt of the Three Feudatories.
12 March 1677: Quanzhou 'lost to the Qing on 12 March 1677'.
5 April 1677: Zhangzhou 'lost to the Qing on 5 April 1677'.
August 1677: 'Haicheng was retaken by Zheng in August 1677'; the town is placed in the Zhangzhou district by the researcher.
10 April 1680: the war on the mainland ends.

wars.name: Siege of Fort Zeelandia
wars.outcome: Ming loyalists' victory: the Dutch East India Company lost Taiwan on 1 February 1662, except Keelung (held to 1668).

wars.name: Qing capture of Xiamen and Kinmen
wars.outcome: The Qing, with Dutch help, took the Zheng bases in November 1663; the Zheng left the mainland coast by spring 1664.

wars.name: Zheng campaigns in the Revolt of the Three Feudatories
wars.outcome: Zheng Jing retook Xiamen, Quanzhou and Zhangzhou in 1674; the tide turned after 1676-1677 and the mainland war ended on 10 April 1680.

wars.name: Battle of Penghu
wars.outcome: Qing victory: Penghu captured on 18 July 1683 and Zheng Keshuang's capitulation of Taiwan followed.

certainty.note: Han settlement on Taiwan's plains had no fixed frontier with aboriginal land (the Qing later required permits beyond the Dajia River); the island coast and the mainland towns are known places, drawn as radii.
